result.what_interviewer_wanted: The interviewer wanted to see a well-rounded understanding of common HTTP status codes across different scenarios (success, client errors like validation and auth, server errors) and how they are used in REST APIs.
result.improved_answer: In REST APIs like the ones I built with FastAPI, I use specific status codes to signal response states clearly: 200 OK for successful requests, 201 Created when a resource is added, and 204 No Content for successful deletions. For client errors, I use 400 Bad Request or 422 for validation failures, 401 Unauthorized when unauthenticated, 403 Forbidden when authenticated but lacking permissions, and 404 Not Found. Finally, 500 Internal Server Error is reserved for unexpected backend failures.
result.one_tip: Expand your knowledge of REST response conventions beyond 200 and 404 to include creation (201), authorization (403), and validation (422) codes.
result.feedback_summary: You covered the standard status codes correctly, but expanding on creation, authorization, and validation codes will make your backend answers much stronger.
result.follow_up_question: In your FastAPI project, how would you handle request validation errors or differentiate between an unauthenticated user (401) and an unauthorized user (403)?
result.transition: Thanks, that gives me a clear idea of how you handle basic HTTP status codes.
